title: Adaptive Frequency Curves & Kernel Fallback Playbook for A100/H100/L4/MI300
abstract: Practical playbook for applying adaptive GPU frequency curves and deterministic kernel fallbacks across our serving fleet. Focused on reducing 95/99p latency regressions while keeping unit cost low. Covers heuristics, per-hardware suggested curves, kernel selection order, KV-cache sizing guidance, observability hooks, and an experiment log.
summary: We propose a runtime policy that adjusts GPU clocks/power caps along a small set of validated frequency points per device family and pairs each frequency point with an ordered kernel candidate list and KV-cache configuration. The goal is to preserve latency SLOs for tail-heavy interactive workloads while avoiding unnecessary power spend. This doc codifies the safe operating bands we tested, the kernel fallthrough ordering we recommend, and the metrics to drive automatic adjustments.
recommendations:
1) Maintain a 3-point frequency curve for each GPU family: ECO (power-sparing), DEFAULT (latency-balanced), PEAK (throughput-bound short bursts).
2) Associate a kernel candidate list ranked by latency for short sequences and by throughput for long sequences; runtime attempts the top kernel and falls back on failure or QoS miss.
3) Use a KV-cache residency heuristic: cold-cache threshold at seq_len <= 64; warm-cache tuning for seq_len 64-1024 with per-layer cache eviction pressure monitored.
4) Bake safety power caps (10-15% below vendor thermal limit) and require SRE approval for persistent raising above PEAK on a cluster.
per_hardware_profiles:
A100 (NVIDIA Ampere)
- ECO: SM clock ~900 MHz, power cap ~160W, use "cutlass-mma-fp16" then "jit-gemm-fp16" fallback. Best for background batch reranks.
- DEFAULT: SM clock ~1095 MHz, power cap ~250W, primary kernel: "flash_attn_v2" (batched attention optimized), fallback: "cutlass-mma-fp16". KV-cache: allocate 0.6x of worst-case memory for common models.
- PEAK: SM clock ~1410 MHz, power cap ~300W, primary kernel: "flash_attn_v3" with prefetching, fallback: "cublasLt-wmma". Use only for short on-demand bursts (<= 10s).

H100 (NVIDIA Hopper)
- ECO: GPU clock gated ~700 MHz, power cap ~200W, primary kernel: "cutlass-wmma-fp16"; fallback: "triton-block-mm".
- DEFAULT: ~1200 MHz, power cap ~320W, primary: "flash_attn_h100" (hopper-optimized), fallback: "cublasLt".
- PEAK: ~1600 MHz, power cap ~400W, enable HBM prefetch; use only with strict thermal-aware placement.

L4 (NVIDIA Ada Lovelace inference GPU)
- ECO: ~400-600 MHz, power cap ~60W, primary kernel: "triton-optim-mm" tuned for int8/INT4.
- DEFAULT: ~900 MHz, power cap ~130W, primary: "int8-quantized-cutlass" then "fp16-fallback". L4 favors quantized kernels for cost-efficiency.

MI300 (AMD CDNA3)
- ECO: conservative freq/power; use "miopen-accel" kernels with fp16 mix.
- DEFAULT: enable ROCm tuned matmul kernels "rocblas-mma" then "miopen-gemm" fallback. Consider slightly higher power caps for sustained long-context workloads.

Notes: exact clocks must be validated per board and vendor BIOS; listed values are starting points from lab runs.
kernel_fallback_order:
Principles: prefer memory-friendly fused kernels (attention fusion, fused softmax) for short tokens; prefer high-throughput GEMM for long sequence/large batch.
Example ordered lists (short_seq <=128): [flash_attn, fused_attention_prefetch, cutlass-mma-fp16, cublasLt-fallback]
Long_seq (>128 or batch>=8): [cutlass-batched-gemm, triton-mm-tiling, cublasLt]
Failure modes that trigger fallback: kernel launch failure, CUDA OOM, observed 99p latency > SLO*1.2 for 3 consecutive windows (30s), or numerical divergence (NaN/Inf).
Rollback policy: if fallback succeeds and meets SLOs for 10 minutes, mark kernel stable and report metric; if not, escalate and possibly reduce clocks/power.
kv_cache_guidance:
Memory estimate: KV bytes per token per layer ~= hidden_size * 2 * bytes_per_element (fp16=2, fp32=4). Example: hidden_size=4096, fp16 => ~16KB/token/layer. For 32 layers and seq_len=1024 => ~512MB.
Heuristics:
- Small models (<=6B): keep full KV in GPU memory by default.
- Large models (>20B): use a tiered KV cache: LRU slices kept in GPU, rest spill to local NVMe with async prefetch.
- Eviction: prefer to evict early layers first (cheap to recompute).
- TTL for prefetched KV pages: 60s of inactivity => evict.
Operational hooks: expose cache_hit_rate, cache_evictions/sec, avg_prefetch_latency as primary observability signals.
scheduling_heuristics:
1) Token-aware scheduling: compute expected per-request token cost via model profile and route to ECO/DEFAULT/PEAK pools.
2) Tail-aware autoscaling: scale up pool size when 95p token latency exceeds SLO for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows; scale down after stable 10 minutes.
3) Hotspot mitigation: if one GPU shows thermal throttling, shift new short-latency requests to sister nodes, allow heavy long-batch jobs to drain.
4) Kernel probe: periodically (off-peak) run microbenchmarks to re-rank kernel candidates for that hardware revision.
experiment_results:
Summary of lab runs (sampled):
- A100 baseline (no adaptive clocks): 95p latency = 210ms, avg throughput 18 tok/s, power 280W.
- A100 DEFAULT curve + kernel ordering: 95p latency = 150ms (-29%), throughput 17 tok/s (-5%), power 250W (-10%).
- H100 DEFAULT with hopper-optimized flash kernel: 95p = 120ms (-35% vs A100 baseline), throughput 26 tok/s, power 330W.
- L4 quantized kernels at DEFAULT: comparable 95p for short contexts, unit cost down ~60% vs A100.
- MI300: better long-seq throughput after enabling rocblas-mma, but needed +8% power cap from vendor defaults to remove oscillatory QoS under sustained load.
Notes: numbers are workload-specific (chatty interactive prompt mix, median seq_len 48). Full CSVs in linked_artifacts.
observability_and_metrics:
Expose these as first-class metrics: per-request kernel_name, kernel_latency_histogram, gpu_clock_state, power_cap, thermal_margin, kv_cache_hit_rate, kv_spill_rate, prefetch_latency_p50/95, kernel_failures/sec.
Alerting: trigger when kernel_failures/sec > 0.5 for 1 minute or kv_spill_rate > 5% for 2 minutes.
Dashboards: per-cluster and per-model views showing trade-offs between energy and tail latency.
safety_and_compliance: All changes to PEAK curves require config review and SRE signoff. Any persistent raise above vendor recommended power caps must have a running card-level telemetry retention for 30 days. For Private deployments we ship a 'gentle' default that never exceeds vendor baseline unless explicitly enabled by admin.
implementation_steps:
1) Add per-hardware profile table to runtime config (three-point curve + kernel_candidates).
2) Implement kernel probe job that runs nightly across instance types and updates ranking.
3) Add KV cache metrics and eviction/refill traces.
4) Implement autoscaler tie-in: 95p-driven scale policy that considers both clock-state and available free memory.
5) Run staged rollout to canary fleet (5% of traffic), measure 7-day stability, then gradual roll to 25/50/100%.
Owners: Samantha Li (design), Miguel Alvarez (kernel integration), Priya Nair (benchmarks), SRE (ops readiness).
open_questions:
- Should we allow per-tenant overriding of PEAK mode? (risk vs revenue).
- Optimal eviction order in mixed-precision KV scenarios—empirically validate layer-cost heuristics.
- Failure-mode SLAs: when to auto-fallback to smaller model vs slower kernel?
- Hardware life-cycle: how do these curves interact with multi-tenant GPU wear and vendor warranties?

notes_to_reviewers: This is a working playbook intended to be prescriptive yet conservative. Please scrutinize the PEAK values (they differ across board revisions) and add any vendor BIOS links or board IDs you have. If you have additional kernel variants (vendor or OSS), add them to the linked_artifacts and the nightly probe will evaluate.
